name: Chicory Blue
lede: Chicory Blue is a soft periwinkle-blue named for the chicory flower.

sections.title: The flower's blue
sections.body:
Our library dates Chicory Blue to Ridgway's 1912 standards, plate XXIV, hue 57*, with Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary giving an earlier first record, 1905, at plate 2, swatch A2 [1]. Chicory is a blue-flowered plant in the daisy family, grown as a coffee substitute and salad green; the flower's own petals are a lighter, more violet blue than this swatch [1].

Our library's nearest everyday match is [[periwinkle]], 3.9 units of ΔE away, with [[blue-bell]], [[lavender]] and [[sky-blue]] listed as other cool near-neighbors [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a close match to Chicory Blue in just 26 of 23,781 paintings (0.11 percent), as photographed, the rarest name, rarer than 64 percent of our named colors [2]. It peaks in the 1800s, in 9 of 8,345 paintings, at 1.5 times the archive's overall rate, and most often plays an accent inside a painting [2]. The earliest dated match, a 1425 work attributed to Sandro Botticelli, is nearly five centuries before the 1912 record, which the archive's thin early coverage explains rather than the color's documented age, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2].
